Definition: from G4195; a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus:--born in Pontus.
BiblicalUsage: Pontikos means a native of Pontus, and Luke uses it once, for Aquila. When Paul finds him at Corinth, he notes that Aquila was born in Pontus and had lately come from Italy with his wife Priscilla.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God writes ordinary people into his story by their birthplace as much as by their deeds, and Aquila's Pontus is part of how the gospel travelled.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
